blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel.

The day's sightseeing, including transfers, lasts 5–6 hours.

The transfer from Bellavista to Cotopaxi takes 3.5 hours.

Overnight altitude: 2,900 m.

Average temperature: +10–15°C.

We set off for the Avenue of the Volcanoes. This impressive natural corridor stretches for about 350 km through the heart of Ecuador.

It owes its name to the German scientist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt. After arriving in Ecuador in the 19th century, he noted the symmetry and near-perfect alignment of the volcanoes, snow-capped mountains and natural landscapes that have long been the main attractions of the Sierra.

About an hour from Quito along the Pan-American Highway stands the distinctive colonial Hacienda San Agustín de Callo. Built on the site of an Inca palace, one of Ecuador's two most important Inca archaeological sites and the northernmost example of imperial-style construction from Cusco, this working hacienda offers an insight into Ecuador's rich and colourful past. Here you can feed the llamas and take photographs with them. Time for lunch (not included).

Continue to another hacienda for the night. The afternoon is free at Hacienda La Ciénega. On the fertile plains of Cotopaxi, surrounded by imposing volcanoes, this is a place where time seems to have stood still. Its colonial setting offers a distinctive experience of Ecuador's highlands.

Accommodation at La Cienega hotel: www.hosterialacienega.com

(Breakfast)
